implementation_notes: JPA is the standard realization: the value class is annotated @Embeddable - instances are stored as an intrinsic part of an owning entity and share the entity's identity, and each persistent property maps to a column of the entity's table - while the owning entity marks the attribute @Embedded. The decompose/recompose pair and the column names are generated by the provider, and @AttributeOverride renames columns when the same embeddable appears twice in one entity (ebookPublisher.name versus paperBackPublisher.name), which JPA requires because the default name-based mapping would collide. Hibernate historically called these components; the concept is the same composition of values.
pitfalls: Using the same embeddable twice without @AttributeOverride/@AssociationOverride maps both occurrences onto the same columns; the specification requires explicit column names in that case.
JPA expects a no-arg constructor on embeddables; Java records and struct-like classes need a custom EmbeddableInstantiator or a @CompositeType instead.
Embeddable types inherit the owning entity's access strategy, so mixing field and property access across the pair changes which members are persistent - annotate explicitly if in doubt.

variants.name: Hibernate aggregate embeddable mapping (@CompositeType / @Struct / JSON)
variants.idiom_name: @CompositeType / @Struct aggregate mapping or JSON column mapping
variants.implementation_notes: Since Hibernate 6.2 an embeddable can also be mapped as a SQL aggregate type instead of as a set of columns: @Struct maps it to a database object type and @JdbcTypeCode to a JSON or XML column, with reads and writes resolving to the proper expression for each attribute. This is the same pattern decision with a different storage target - the value still has no identity and no table, but it is one column or one user-defined type rather than N columns, which is what you want when the database supports the type and the value is not filtered column-wise. Note the documented limits: association mappings are not supported in aggregate mappings, and column order inside a @Struct follows the embeddable's attribute order, so the DDL must match.
pitfalls: Aggregate mappings do not support association mappings inside the embeddable, so a value that needs a @ManyToOne cannot use this variant.

For @Struct the column order in the DDL must match the order Hibernate expects (alphabetical by attribute name, or the order given by @Struct(attributes = ...)), otherwise the aggregate is silently misread.
A JSON-mapped value loses column-level constraints and partial predicates - the trade-off is exactly the one Embedded Value was chosen to avoid, so pick it deliberately.
